decisions.rationale: The item directly tests the source-defined landing-site condition of a level location with no surrounding or overhead obstacle. Q090 tests the flight-area safety margin and Q119 tests compass-error structures, so the proposition is materially distinct.
The end-to-end safety-management lifecycle from pre-takeoff through post-landing is explicit in the source and distinct from Q091 constraint integration and Q121 anticipated-condition checks.
The source explicitly states that risk-management thinking remains applicable outside Category III. Existing canonical items test components of risk assessment, not this applicability boundary.

Fail closed on source support. The source states that risk may be reduced through probability-reduction measures and/or consequence-mitigation measures, but it does not explicitly require every risk decision to consider both measure classes before selecting controls. The candidate makes that combined-review duty answer-defining and therefore overstates the cited proposition relative to Q009/Q010.
High-pressure clockwise outward circulation, central subsidence and generally fair weather are explicit and are the distinct counterpart to Q264's low-pressure circulation.
The west-high/east-low winter pattern and Sea-of-Japan snowfall consequence are source-defined and absent from the canonical bank.
The surface-intersection definition of a front is explicit and distinct from existing items on individual cold, warm and stationary-front behavior.
Occluded-front formation by a cold front catching a warm front and subsequent low-pressure weakening are both explicit and not otherwise tested.

The item binds spring/autumn air-mass transition to a stationary boundary, prolonged rain, low cloud base and visibility degradation. Q266 only tests stationary-front persistence/long rain, so the causal weather-to-operational-risk path is materially distinct.

Semantic collision/low incremental value. Q266 already defines stationary fronts and explicitly identifies Baiu and autumn-rain fronts as examples that bring prolonged rain. Recasting Baiu as the prominent prolonged/heavy-rain stationary-front subtype adds too little solving-rule distinctness for the 400-target quality floor.
The high-to-low pressure direction of horizontal air flow is a foundational explicit wind proposition not tested by Q263's isobar-spacing strength rule or Q264's low-pressure circulation.
The wind-direction naming convention tests origin-versus-destination interpretation and is distinct from sea/land wind and mountain/valley wind direction-change questions.
The approximately 4 km microburst classification boundary and potentially stronger downdraft characteristic are source-defined; Q129 tests short duration/local detectability instead.

Tier B PASS. The source explicitly requires pre-start confirmation that weather will not interfere from takeoff through landing. Q093 tests information-source selection and Q096/Q126 test already-present fog/thunder. This candidate changes the temporal decision boundary and reasoning path.

The elevated proficiency and safety-awareness requirement for aircraft at or above 25 kg follows explicitly from greater accident consequence and differs from inertia/avoidance and emergency-landing-area questions.
Large-aircraft noise and route-neighborhood consideration are explicit. Q163 tests power-source-related noise differences, not size-related route impact.
Tier B PASS. GNSS anomaly is a separate failure trigger from Q139 radio-link loss, with its own source-defined response branch of position hold, safe auto-landing or alternative positioning.

Tier B PASS. Battery voltage/capacity/temperature abnormality defines a separate failure branch requiring smoke/fire prevention plus return or safe landing; Q045 only covers low-temperature endurance reduction.

Tier B PASS. Q154 tests the certified third-party-harm-prevention function as the baseline no-assistant BVLOS requirement; this item tests the source's explicit controlled-area/continuous-monitoring exception boundary.

Tier B PASS. The explicit requirement to retain ground awareness of aircraft location even after an abnormal forced landing changes the lifecycle state relative to Q138's bundled normal/abnormal equipment requirement and Q141's telemetry/path-delta checks.
